newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dow Chemical/China in talks to build petchem plant.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical/China in talks to build petchem plant.

text.p: The Dow Chemical Co said on Tuesday it was holding talks with China's SINOPEC to build a petrochemical plant which will include a 600,000 tonne-per-year naphtha cracker.

The company hoped to sign a letter of intent with the state-owned refining and petrochemical company in the first half of 1997, chief executive officer William Stavropoulos told a news conference in Singapore.
The company is planning various Asian projects worth around $300 million during the rest of the decade.
Stavropoulos said sales from the company's Asian interest would grow by 2005 to 20 percent of global turnover from the current 13 percent. Dow's 1995 turnover was $20.2 billion.

Stavropoulos, who is also president of the company, said the petrochemical complex would be situated in Tianjin, in northern China. He said the initial idea on the project included the naphtha cracker and a "major" downstream petrochemicals plant.
Dow also plans a polyurethane plant in Guangzhou, southern China, geared to both domestic and export markets.
In September, Dow signed a letter of intent with Yangzi Petrochemical Co to build a polyethylene terephthalate plant -- a plastic resin used for packaging.
In August, the China Daily newspaper reported that Dow planned investments totalling $4 billion to build an ethylene plant at Tianjin.
